key_insight: A physics-informed neural network couples flow prediction and blade-shape updates to translate target surface pressures into turbine-blade geometry changes.
engineering_relevance: The method offers an inverse-design route for tailoring turbine-blade aerodynamic loading to experimental-origin pressure targets.
method: Constrain the flow with the 2D steady compressible Euler equations.
Use pressure-target continuation and alternate geometry updates with flow re-adaptation.
Optimize differentiable blade-surface positions and orientations.
evidence_signal: On the LS89 cascade with 28 experimental-derived pressure targets, final pressure-side and suction-side RMS errors were 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure; independent SharC verification reproduced the main pressure trends.
watch_item: The inviscid 2D formulation does not establish viscous or turbulent performance, and trailing-edge pressure differences remain.
paper_title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
